title: New Study Reveals Indonesian Youth Show Strong Confidence, But Seek More Real-World Experience
summary: 99% want more exposure to the workplace, even as Indonesia records some of Asia Pacific's strongest self-reported readiness scores
body_markdown:
Jakarta, Indonesia, August 26, 2026 — Federal Express Corporation (FedEx), one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, and Junior Achievement (JA), one of the world’s largest youth-serving nonprofits, released findings from[Shaping Tomorrow’s Workforce – Asia Pacific Youth Insights](https://www.jaasiapacific.org/2026-itc-apac-finals)


, a new study jointly commissioned by FedEx and JA and published by the JA Institute.


Surveying over 4,200 young people aged 15 to 22 across ten Asia Pacific markets, including 552 respondents in Indonesia, the study offers timely insights into how prepared they feel for future careers, with a focus on practical and entrepreneurial capabilities, global trade knowledge and AI readiness.


The study coincides with the 20th year of the FedEx/JA International Trade Challenge (ITC), marking two decades of collaborative effort to advance entrepreneurship education across Asia Pacific. Since 2007, the program has reached more than 54,000 students across Asia Pacific, helping them build practical business, problem-solving, and cross-cultural collaboration skills through real-world learning experiences focused on global trade.


In Indonesia, nearly all respondents (99%) want their education to provide greater exposure to how the working world operates, significantly above the Asia Pacific result of 97%. Problem-solving and critical thinking emerged as the country’s top-ranked capabilities for the next 10 to 15 years.


“Indonesian youth have incredible energy, creativity and adaptability. They don’t just want to learn theory; they also want opportunities to apply their talents in real business environments,” said Garrick Thompson, managing director, FedEx Indonesia. “As technology such as AI and cross-border trade reshape the future, students need practical skills beyond the classroom. Through our partnership with Junior Achievement, FedEx is proud to help young Indonesians gain real-world business experience. We are committed to preparing the next generation to succeed in the global economy.”


**Indonesian Youth Combine Entrepreneurial Confidence with Demand for Practical Experience**
The report highlights that Indonesian youth want formal education to place greater emphasis on capabilities they can apply as the workplace changes, with particular demand for stronger links between the classroom and the world of work.


Indonesian respondents also report higher-than-regional confidence across several transferable capabilities:


• 78% feel confident generating new ideas or solutions, compared with 61% across Asia Pacific.
• 72% feel confident taking action on something new without being told or asked, compared with 60% regionally.
• 73% feel confident adapting quickly when plans change, compared with 62% regionally.
• 69% feel confident working independently and making decisions without significant guidance, compared with 59% regionally.


These self-reported findings point to a strong foundation of initiative and adaptability.


However, confidence does not always translate into comfort with less structured work: only 43% of Indonesian respondents feel comfortable working without a fixed routine, compared with 56% across Asia Pacific.


**Youth See Entrepreneurial Thinking as Valuable Across Careers**
The need to turn transferable skills into action is also reflected in how Indonesian youth perceive entrepreneurial thinking: 95% agree that an entrepreneurial mindset can help people succeed in any job, compared with 85% across Asia Pacific.


Indonesian respondents also give formal education relatively strong credit for their career preparation. On average, they estimate that formal education will provide approximately 81% of what they need to succeed in their future careers, compared with 69% across Asia Pacific. The finding suggests that the demand for more workplace exposure is a call to build on formal education, rather than replace it.


**Education Must Keep Pace with AI and an Interconnected Economy**
Beyond entrepreneurial capabilities, the study also highlights the importance of preparing young people to navigate an AI-enabled and increasingly interconnected economy. While Indonesian youth recognize the relevance of these capabilities, opportunities remain to strengthen their practical application:


• 94% believe understanding how business works across countries will be relevant to their future careers, but only 69% say their school or university has taught them how cross-border trade works.
• 84% believe they will need to work alongside AI, but only 70% feel their education is preparing them to use it in a real working environment.
• Indonesian youth are also more likely than the regional average to prioritize digital and technology skills in the curriculum, at 18% compared with 12% across Asia Pacific.


Across Asia Pacific, self-directed experimentation is the most commonly cited source of AI learning, at 42%, indicating that young people are looking beyond formal education to develop their capabilities.


**Nurturing a Future-Ready Generation**
“The most striking finding from this study is that young people are asking for more exposure to the workplace and real-world experience. As youth unemployment in Asia Pacific stands at almost 14% now, much higher than the adult rate, and the AI adoption divide continues to widen, we cannot assume that talent alone will be enough for young people to succeed. They need opportunities to build practical skills, gain confidence, and understand how work is evolving,” said Vivek Kumar, President and Chief Executive Officer of JA Asia Pacific. “Last year, JA Asia Pacific helped more than 5 million young people prepare for the workplace, thanks to the commitment of our partner schools, teachers, volunteers, and long-standing corporate supporters such as FedEx. Our collective responsibility now is to ensure that every young person has a fair chance to thrive in the economy of the future.”


The findings also indicate where this support can have the greatest impact: helping young people use AI responsibly, navigate less structured business challenges and apply classroom knowledge in real-world situations. Industry-led, locally relevant programs can build the judgement, adaptability and commercial understanding needed by the region’s future entrepreneurs, employees and business leaders.


For more insights on the future-ready skills that APAC youth need,[check out the full “Shaping Tomorrow’s Workforce: Asia Pacific Youth Insights” report](https://www.jaasiapacific.org/2026-itc-apac-finals)


.


**About the Findings**
The insights in this release are drawn from Shaping Tomorrow’s Workforce – Asia Pacific Youth Insights,commissioned by FedEx and JA Asia Pacific, published by JA Institute, and conducted by Bolt Insight. The online quantitative survey was conducted between June and July 2026 among 4,219 young people aged 15 to 22 across ten Asia Pacific markets: China, Hong Kong SAR, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, the Republic of Korea, Thailand and Vietnam.


**About Federal Express Corporation**
Federal Express Corporation is one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, providing fast and reliable delivery to more than 220 countries and territories. Federal Express Corporation uses a global air-and-ground network to speed delivery of time-sensitive shipments by a definite time and date.


**About JA Asia Pacific**
Started in 1919 to bridge the gap between classrooms and workplaces, JA Worldwide is one of the world’s oldest and most impactful youth-serving NGOs. Junior Achievement (JA) is dedicated to hands-on, immersive learning in work readiness, financial health, entrepreneurship, STEM, sustainability, and more. JA Worldwide has been nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize every year since 2022. Delivering more than 23 million student experiences each year in over 100 countries, JA Worldwide is one of few organizations with the scale, experience, and passion to build a brighter future for the next generation of innovators, entrepreneurs, and leaders.


In 2025, JA Asia Pacific, a Member of JA Worldwide, reached more than 5 million students, spanning 14 markets, and engaged more than 66,000 teachers and volunteers in Asia Pacific alone.
Learn more about us here:[www.jaasiapacific.org](http://www.jaasiapacific.org/)


**About JA Institute**
The JA Institute is the research, insights, and thought leadership arm of Junior Achievement (JA), dedicated to producing research on cost-effective ways to implement learning experiences, scale JA’s footprint, introduce innovation, and measure our effectiveness and impact; and translating research into thought leadership that strengthens our youth-advocacy efforts and helps JA lead global conversations.


Learn more about us here:[https://www.ja.institute/](https://www.ja.institute/)
